title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement correctly tells an agent apart from a workflow?

options.text: An agent runs on a larger, more capable model, while a workflow runs on a smaller one
In an agent the model decides the steps and when to stop; in a workflow, code fixed beforehand sets them
A workflow never calls a language model, while an agent calls one at every step
An agent needs several different models working together, while a workflow needs only one

items.stem: Which of these makerspace features is a workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: The model gets a booking goal plus the tools check_calendar and book_machine, and chooses its own calls until it decides it is done
The model answers a question by choosing between search_manuals and check_calendar, and searches again if the first result is thin
Code looks up the booking, makes one model call to write the confirmation text, then sends it, in that order for every request
The model reads the student's message and decides which tools to use, in what order, and how many times to use them

items.stem: The assistant gets 40 requests a day. 30 are booking confirmations whose steps never vary; a fixed workflow handles each with exactly 2 model calls. The other 10 are open-ended troubleshooting requests whose steps depend on what is found along the way; an agent handles each with an average of 5 model calls. If each kind of request uses the design that suits it, how many model calls does the assistant make per day in total?

Each booking always needs three actions in one required sequence: check the student's training record, check the calendar, then write the booking. Judged on predictability and cost, which choice fits best?

options.text: A fixed workflow: the three steps never vary, so code can run them for predictable cost and simple testing
An agent: a flexible system handles bookings well, and its extra model calls are a small price for that
An agent: choosing the order itself lets the model finish in fewer calls than a fixed order would
A fixed workflow: code can also handle unplanned booking questions by rewriting its own steps as it goes

items.stem: A student writes: "My part came out warped on the 3D printer. Find out why and book a reprint." Which steps are needed depends on what the assistant finds in the manuals and the printer's logs. Which design fits best?

options.text: A fixed workflow, because it costs less per request and the sponsor's model budget is small
A fixed workflow, because one set sequence of manual search, log check and booking is more reliable
An agent, because the model must pick each next step from what the earlier results show
An agent, because a model that writes the final answer to the student counts as an agent

items.stem: In a proposed design, one model call reads each student message and outputs a single label, "manual_question" or "booking". Code then runs a pipeline the team wrote for that label, and each pipeline's steps never change. Judged by who owns the control flow, which description is best?

options.text: A workflow: the code owns the sequence, and the model only picks among paths prepared in advance
An agent: the model's label decides which steps happen next, so the model steers the process
An agent: a language model reads the request, and that alone is enough to make a system an agent
Neither: a single model call is too small to count as either design
